messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Serbian (Latin script), guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Serbian (Latin script) line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|--------------------|------------------|--------| | In | locative preposition introducing “all parts” | U | “in” | OK | | tutte | universal quantifier “all” | svim | “all” (plural, locative) | OK | | parti | noun “parts” (the set of divisions) | delovima | “parts” (locative plural) | OK | | impera | verb “governs” (exerts rule) | vlada | “governs” | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction | i | “and” | OK | | quivi | adverb “there” (place of reign) | tamo | “there” | OK | | regge | verb “reigns” (holds sovereign authority) | reinira | “reigns” | OK | | quivi | adverb “there” (place of city) | tamo | “there” | OK | | è | copular verb “is” (asserts existence) | je | “is” | OK | | la | definite article (fem. sing.) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | sua | possessive adjective “His” (ownership) | njegov | “his” | OK | | città | noun “city” (urban domain) | grad | “city” | OK | | e | conjunction “and” | i | “and” | OK | | l'alto | adjective “lofty” (with article) | visoko | “lofty” | OK | | seggio | noun “seat” (throne) | prijestolje | “seat” | OK | | oh | interjection “O” (vocative) | o | “O” | OK | | felice | adjective “happy” (state of the chosen) | srećni | “happy” | OK | | colui | pronoun “he” (the one) | onaj | “that one” | OK | | cu' | relative pronoun “whom” (introduces clause) | koga | “whom” | OK | | ivi | adverb “there/thereto” (locative of election) | tamo | “there” | OK | | elege | verb “elects” (selects) | izabire | “elects” | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: *la* – the Italian definite article has no counterpart in Serbian and is naturally omitted. - Implicitly, the article contained in *l'alto* is also omitted (Serbian does not use an article before adjectives), but the adjective itself (*visoko*) is correctly rendered, so no separate status flag is needed.
All other source tokens are represented accurately, with correct grammatical agreement and meaning.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Serbian (Latin script) script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Serbian (Latin script) text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
